findings.text:
The comment promises "nothing ambient leaks", but only `HOME`/`PATH` are overridden; inherited
`REQ_GATE_BIN` (which `check.sh` is documented to honour) would bypass the stub `cargo` and run the
real `req` against an empty fixture, and `REQ_ROOT`/`CARGO_HOME`/`RUSTUP_HOME` can change what the
copied script resolves. The sibling `check_sh_env` already removes `REQ_ROOT` for exactly this
reason — clear the same variables here so the fixture is the same tree in CI and locally.
findings.title: Make gate-script fixture hermetic
findings.code:
std::process::Command::new("bash")
    .arg(fixture.path().join("scripts/check.sh"))
    .current_dir(fixture.path())
    .env("HOME", fixture.path().join("home"))
    .env(
        "PATH",
        format!("{}:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin", bin.display()),
    )
    .output()
    .expect("runs the copied scripts/check.sh")

findings.text: The new sentence says `dependencies_decided` refuses (exit 3) whenever a declared line fails to decide "every key an applying claim depends on". That is not what the gate does: only `corpus_set` is dependency-guarded (REQ-0009/10/11 refine REQ-0008). Dropping `runs`, `set`, `deployment_mode`, or `field` from a line leaves the affected claim undecided while the gate still exits 0 — which is precisely why `tests/release_gate.rs::every_declared_release_is_gate_green` has to assert `, 0 undecided` explicitly. The `.req/variants` bullet a few lines below states the opposite ("the gate will *not* tell you when one does not"), so the two passages now contradict each other, and a developer could drop a key believing the gate would catch it.
findings.title: Misleading gate guarantee

findings.text: This assertion cannot fail: the gate's headline is always `# Release gate: {applying} applying claim(s), {undecided} undecided (an undecided claim is never treated as absent)` (`src/gate.rs`), so `contains("undecided")` is true even for `0 undecided` — the very case this negative-direction test exists to reject. Pin the mechanism the doc describes instead: the `dependencies_decided` policy refusing (REQ-0009 -> REQ-0008 undecided), or the measured count `16 applying claim(s), 5 undecided`.
findings.title: test

findings.text:
`-r` is true for a readable *directory*, so a directory named `.req/variants` passes this guard and
then the `done < "$PWD/.req/variants"` redirection fails, leaving `variants_gated` at 0 and printing
the misleading "declares no release" message the loop was meant to prevent. Requiring a regular file
routes that case to the `else` branch, whose "missing or unreadable" message names the real cause.
findings.title: Guard release list as regular file
